source_name: Fio banka – Investiční zpravodajství (investment research)
why_relevant: Fio banka runs an in-house analyst team publishing Czech-language investment commentary, and is the house behind the Akcie.cz / e-Broker / RM-SYSTÉM ecosystem identified above. Tracking Fio directly separates its primary research output from the aggregated form it takes on Akcie.cz.

source_name: Roklen24 – finanční zpravodajství (now FX-focused)
why_relevant: Named in the cell seed as a Czech financial news source. Confirmed live and published by Roklen Holding a.s., but the current site is materially narrower than the seed assumes: it is now an FX/currency-pair education and commentary property with an economic calendar, and does NOT carry bank ratings or traditional sell-side analyst research. Retained at low priority for its central-bank-decision calendar only.

source_name: ESMA – Credit Rating Agencies supervision hub
why_relevant: Confirmed live. ESMA registers and supervises every credit rating agency operating in the EU, so this page is the authoritative pointer to which CRAs may legally rate Czech banks — including smaller EU agencies beyond the big three that the seed query would never surface. It also publishes annual CRA market-share calculations, which is a cheap way to discover under-tracked raters.

source_name: bne IntelliNews - Central Europe / Czech Republic desk
why_relevant: Homepage fetch confirmed a Central Europe desk that explicitly lists Czech Republic alongside Hungary, Poland, Slovakia, Slovenia and the Baltics, with News / Data / Features / Opinion verticals. bne is the main English-language business wire for CEE and routinely summarises Czech bank results, ownership changes and regulatory events for a foreign-investor audience, effectively acting as the English translation layer for Czech-only announcements.

source_name: Emerging Europe
why_relevant: Independent English-language CEE platform (operated by Reinvantage, publishing since 2012). Its on-site search for 'Czech bank' returned real Czech banking and fintech articles, confirming genuine Czech coverage even though no Czech tag page appears in the top navigation. Useful for fintech/challenger-bank expansion stories, bank taxation debates and monetary-policy context that Czech-language outlets cover only domestically.

source_name: Finextra Research
why_relevant: Highest-volume English fintech/payments trade news source (site reports ~154k stories) with a dedicated payments channel plus regulation, crypto, identity, security and AI channels, and a separate 'company updates' feed that republishes vendor and bank press releases. This is the main English channel where Czech payment-scheme, acquiring, instant-payments and bank-technology announcements surface for an international audience.

source_name: Reuters
why_relevant: Primary international wire for Czech bank earnings, M&A, licence and supervisory events; typically the first English rendering of a Czech-language regulatory filing or CNB decision, and the version cited by other outlets. Core to the English half of the mandated bilingual sweep for the CZ A1 workstream.

source_name: Bloomberg
why_relevant: Second core international wire for Czech bank and payments deal flow, valuation context and cross-border M&A framing aimed at institutional investors. Frequently carries exclusives on Czech financial-sector ownership changes ahead of local outlets.

source_name: The Banker (FT Specialist)
why_relevant: FT-group specialist banking title; publishes the Top 1000 World Banks ranking and country/regional bank profiles, which are among the few English-language comparative datasets placing Czech banks against CEE peers. Valuable for benchmarking and for annual-report-derived balance-sheet comparisons.

source_name: Prague Morning - Politics & Economics
why_relevant: Self-described largest English-language media outlet in the Czech Republic. Its Politics & Economics desk carries Czech corporate and economic news in English (observed topics include EU budget, wage and household-cost stories, and Czech companies in global rankings), making it a secondary translation channel for Czech banking and payments announcements aimed at the expatriate and foreign-business audience.

source_name: CTK - Czech News Agency, foreign/English service
why_relevant: The national news agency and the upstream origin of most Czech financial news that international outlets republish. Its English-language service for foreign clients covers political, business and economic reporting, and it also runs a press-release distribution service (CTK Connect / Protext) plus an Infobank archive - so it is simultaneously the wire, the press-release pipe and the archive. Identifying it maps the supply chain behind everything else in this cell.

source_name: The Paypers
why_relevant: Amsterdam-based global payments and fintech news platform with explicit coverage of payments, ecommerce, fraud, crypto/CBDC, regulation and M&A. Complements Finextra for European payments-market events touching Czech acquirers, PSPs, licence grants and cross-border payment deals; also publishes reference reports that map market participants.

source_name: Retail Banker International (GlobalData / Verdict)
why_relevant: Specialist English retail-banking trade title covering strategy, regulation, products, distribution and channel technology, backed by GlobalData's deals/M&A and company-intelligence databases. Relevant to A1 because it aggregates bank announcements and deal records into a structured English layer that can be filtered for Czech institutions.

source_name: Central Banking (Infopro Digital)
why_relevant: Specialist English coverage of central banks and financial regulators, with explicit sections for monetary policy, financial stability and micro-prudential supervision, payments systems, CBDC, and fintech/regtech/suptech. This is the natural English channel for Czech National Bank policy, supervision and payment-system developments that would otherwise only appear in Czech, and it also runs benchmarking data and awards.

source_name: Global Finance Magazine
why_relevant: Publishes country-level financial data and rankings for 180+ nations plus annual Best Bank / Best Digital Bank / Best Treasury and Cash Management awards broken out by country, which produce recurring English-language snapshots naming leading Czech banks. Useful as a low-effort annual benchmark and as a pointer to which Czech institutions are visible internationally.

source_name: PYMNTS
why_relevant: High-volume English payments publication with an EMEA desk and cross-border payments coverage. Included for completeness of the English payments layer, but an on-site search for 'Czech' returned mostly EU-wide and Poland-centric items with no Czech-focused article on the first page - so Czech relevance is incidental rather than systematic.

source_name: MarketScreener (English aggregator of listed-bank news)
why_relevant: Aggregates company news, regulatory filings and analyst commentary per listed issuer in English, including Prague Stock Exchange-listed banks. Valuable as a pointer layer: a per-company news timeline that reveals which English outlets and which primary disclosures exist for a given Czech bank, without having to guess each issuer's IR page.

source_name: CEE Legal Matters
why_relevant: English-language legal-market publication for Central and Eastern Europe with country desks. Law-firm deal announcements are an early and unusually precise English record of Czech banking and payments M&A, licence transfers and financing transactions - often naming parties and structures before or instead of mainstream coverage.

source_name: FinTech Futures
why_relevant: English banking-technology and fintech trade title (long-running, formerly Banking Technology). Typical channel for core-banking, card-processing and payments-vendor contract wins involving Czech banks - the kind of supplier-side announcement that rarely appears in mainstream Czech media but matters for a payments-technology market view.

source_name: ČNB — Přehled odkazů na webové stránky družstevních záložen obsahující povinně uveřejňované informace
why_relevant: Same statutory template applied to the credit-union tier (spořitelní a úvěrní družstva) — institutions that publish essentially nothing else structured. Enumerated six: Artesa, Citfin spořitelní družstvo, České spořitelní družstvo, NEY spořitelní družstvo, Peněžní dům, Podnikatelská družstevní záložna, each with a deep link. Completes the deposit-taking universe beyond banks.

source_name: ČNB — Přehled odkazů na webové stránky finančních holdingových osob obsahující povinně uveřejňované informace
why_relevant: Captures the consolidating-group layer above the banks — the level at which CRR Part Eight disclosure is actually made for a group. Listed CREDITAS B.V. (creditasgroup.cz/povinne-uverejnovane-informace) and PPF Financial Holdings a.s. Group-level Pillar 3 is where consolidated capital, MREL and ownership chains become visible for otherwise opaque privately-held Czech banking groups.

source_name: ČNB — Informační povinnosti subjektů finančního trhu (hub of all disclosure link-indexes)
why_relevant: Parent hub that enumerates six separate 'Přehled odkazů na webové stránky…' indexes — banks, credit unions, financial holding companies, investment companies (IS), non-bank securities dealers (OCP), pension companies — plus reporting-obligation pages for intermediaries, issuers and non-bank credit providers. Snowballing this one page yielded three link-indexes the seed queries did not surface; it is the cheapest way to detect a *new* index appearing.

source_name: ČNB — Přehled odkazů na webové stránky obchodníků s cennými papíry (nebanky) obsahující povinně uveřejňované informace
why_relevant: Adjacent tier of the same Decree 163/2014 disclosure family, covering ~35 non-bank investment firms — several of which are payments/FX-relevant actors (AKCENTA CZ, Citfin - Finanční trhy, BH Securities, ATLANTIK finanční trhy, Amundi CZ). Since 1.4.2021 their basis moved to Part Six of Regulation (EU) 2019/2033 (IFR) plus §16a of Act 256/2004 Sb., so it is a separate but structurally identical machine-comparable set.

source_name: ČNB — Vyhláška č. 163/2014 Sb. (výkon činnosti bank, spořitelních a úvěrních družstev a OCP) — legal texts and consolidated version
why_relevant: Defines the schema of the whole cell: Part Five plus Annex 10 prescribed the quarterly template (capital and capital adequacy, exposures, shareholder/ownership structure, organisational chart, number of branches and employees) and mandated publication in Czech, in a folder labelled 'Povinně uveřejňované informace', as unlocked downloadable xls/xlsx. Needed to write a stable parser and to interpret column semantics across banks and across time (amendments 392/2017 and 354/2021 changed the annexes).

source_name: EBA Pillar 3 Data Hub (P3DH) / European Data Access Portal (EDAP)
why_relevant: The successor regime to this cell. Part Five and Annexes 10/13 of Decree 163/2014 were repealed with effect from 1.7.2025 and prudential disclosure is being centralised at the EBA under CRR3 Arts. 433/434/434a; the hub is live and holds Pillar 3 data for EEA institutions in a harmonised form. If it delivers, it replaces 25+ individual Czech bank scrapes with one machine-readable feed and makes CZ banks comparable to peers EEA-wide. Must be tracked in parallel with the national pages during the transition.

source_name: Komerční banka — Informace o bance (povinně uveřejňované informace)
why_relevant: KB's dedicated quarterly dataset page, the cleanest example of the cell's canonical artefact: quarterly 'Informace o bance' packages under Decree 163/2014 and CRR, served as ZIP bundles and XLSX (PDF pre-2014), with an unbroken archive from Q3 2003 to Q4 2025. A 22-year machine-comparable time series for the second-largest Czech bank, separate from the IR pages.

source_name: Česká spořitelna — Povinné informace v souladu s vyhláškou (Dokumenty ke stažení)
why_relevant: Largest Czech bank by clients; its statutory quarterly disclosures sit inside a generic 'Dokumenty ke stažení' document hub rather than on the IR site — exactly the low-traffic legal corner this cell targets. The ČNB index points only at the hub root; the disclosure set is behind an in-page tab/anchor.

source_name: ČSOB Hypoteční banka — Povinně uveřejňované informace
why_relevant: Hypoteční banka is listed in the ČNB index under its old name and old domain (hypotecnibanka.cz) but has been rebranded to ČSOB Hypoteční banka on csobhypotecni.cz while remaining a separately disclosing licensed bank. It is the largest dedicated Czech mortgage lender, so its standalone quarterly set is the only structured view of that book outside ČSOB consolidated numbers.

source_name: MONETA — Dceřiné společnosti disclosure hub (MONETA Stavební Spořitelna, MONETA Auto, MONETA Leasing, Wüstenrot hypoteční banka)
why_relevant: Aggregates the statutory disclosure sets of MONETA's regulated subsidiaries in one place, including MONETA Stavební Spořitelna (the ČNB-listed entity) and Wüstenrot hypoteční banka — the latter does not appear in the ČNB bank link-index, so this page is the only route found to its subsidiary-level disclosures.

source_name: UniCredit Bank Czech Republic and Slovakia — Povinné údaje o bance
why_relevant: One of the four largest Czech banks and a cross-border CZ/SK entity, so its statutory Czech quarterly set is the only place where the Czech-perimeter view of the merged CZ+SK bank is disclosed in the standard national template. Local term used on the page itself is 'povinné údaje o bance', a variant worth adding to the glossary.

source_name: Fio banka — Hospodářské výsledky / čtvrtletní povinně uveřejňované informace
why_relevant: Unlisted, domestically owned retail/brokerage bank with no equity IR function — the statutory quarterly XLSX set is effectively its only structured public financial reporting. Confirmed still running post-repeal: multi-annex XLSX quarterly filings with Q4 2025 published 30.4.2026 and H1 2026 following, on a fixed May/Aug/Nov/Apr cadence, archive to 2006, plus §32g non-financial reporting and audit-committee composition.

source_name: Air Bank a.s. — Dokumenty ke stažení, záložka 'Povinně uveřejňované informace'
why_relevant: PPF-group digital retail bank with no listed equity; its statutory quarterly disclosures live behind a tab on a general customer-documents page (tabs: Formuláře / Ke smlouvě / Povinně uveřejňované informace / Osobní údaje / Podnikatelé) — a textbook 'low-traffic legal corner'. Consolidated annual reports are served from a predictable /file-download/ path.

source_name: J&T BANKA, a.s. — Informační povinnost
why_relevant: Private-banking/investment bank; its 'Informační povinnost' index bundles the statutory disclosures with annual and half-year reports, consolidated information, PSD2 dedicated-interface availability and performance statistics, and merger/division/business-transfer notices — the PSD2 API uptime statistics make this page doubly relevant to the payments side of the run. Consolidated quarterly PDFs are served from a Kentico CDN (assets-eu-01.kc-usercontent.com) with stable filename patterns (ZI_JTBA_YYYYMM.pdf).

source_name: PPF banka a.s. — Údaje uveřejňované čtvrtletně
why_relevant: Recovered URL for a wholesale/private bank whose ČNB-listed path (/cz/servis-pro-investory-a-analytiky/informacni-povinnosti/) now 404s after a site migration to /cs/dokumenty/. Confirmed still publishing post-repeal: XLSX 'příloha 4/5' files, archive from 2014, latest 30.6.2026 posted 5.8.2026. Unlisted PPF-group bank with minimal other structured reporting.

source_name: Národní rozvojová banka (ex-ČMZRB) — Povinně uveřejňované informace
why_relevant: State-owned promotional bank. Its disclosure corner is unusually rich because it stacks three regimes: the ex-163/2014 quarterly set (URL slugs still read 'vyhlaska-cnb-c-163-2014-sb-...-ctvrtleti-YYYY'), CRR Part Eight annual bank information, Act 90/2012 corporate disclosures and — uniquely among banks — Act 106/1999 Sb. freedom-of-information duties, plus ČBA Standard No. 31. Also carries an explicit archive sub-page. Legacy cmzrb.cz URLs still resolve to the same tree.

source_name: Česká exportní banka — Pravidelné čtvrtletní informace
why_relevant: State export-credit bank. Recovered after the ČNB-listed URL 404'd. Confirmed a near-complete quarterly series from 31.3.2012 to 30.6.2026 in XLSX (older XLS/PDF), plus supplementary year-end reports under §11b odst. 6 zákona o bankách — i.e. it continued publishing well past the 1.7.2025 repeal.

source_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited, Prague Branch — Povinně uveřejňované informace
why_relevant: Non-EEA third-country branch, which is precisely why it is in scope: EEA-passported branches (mBank, Citibank Europe, ING, BNP, Deutsche, Oberbank) are exempt, so ICBC Prague's quarterly XLSX set is one of only two windows into a third-country bank's Czech operation. Confirmed quarterly Czech-language XLSX/XLS with an archive back to 2017 and filings through 31.12.2025, on a CRR Part Eight basis.

source_name: Bank of Communications Co., Ltd., Prague Branch — mandatory disclosures
why_relevant: The second third-country branch in the ČNB index. Unusually, disclosures are surfaced in English and Chinese rather than Czech, and are hosted on the parent group's global CMS rather than a local domain — a reminder that the cell's 'always in Czech, always on the local site' assumption has exceptions. Quarterly filings observed from Q3 2022 to Q3 2025 with a ~2-3 month lag.

source_name: Raiffeisen stavební spořitelna — Dokumenty / povinně uveřejňované informace
why_relevant: Building society (stavební spořitelna) tier of the same template. The ČNB-listed URL 301-redirects into /dokumenty/. Confirmed ~218 indexed mandatory-disclosure records: quarterly XLSX at 31.3/30.6/30.9/31.12 through mid-2026, annual reports CZ+EN, an explicit MREL/TLAC disclosure stream, and ČBA-standard filings.

source_name: Buřinka — Stavební spořitelna České spořitelny — Povinně uveřejňované informace
why_relevant: Building society in the Erste/Česká spořitelna group. The ČNB index still points at burinka.cz, which now 301-redirects to burinka.csas.cz — the disclosure section has migrated to the parent bank's domain, an early sign of the group-consolidation pattern also visible at KB/Modrá pyramida and ČSOB/ČMSS. Disclosures made under the ČNB decree regime.

source_name: ČSOB Stavební spořitelna (ex-ČMSS) — Informace dle vyhlášky ČNB
why_relevant: Largest Czech building society. The ČNB index still lists cmss.cz, whose HTTPS endpoint refused connection outright, while the entity has been rebranded onto csobstavebni.cz — a rebrand-plus-domain-move that the regulator's index has not tracked. Proposed corrected URL follows the same slug used on the legacy domain.

source_name: Modrá pyramida stavební spořitelna — Dokumenty
why_relevant: KB-group building society, still a separate legal entity with its own disclosure duty (confirmed: the company persists in statutory form and in client documentation even after product consolidation into KB and rebranding of branches to 'KB Poradenská místa' in 2025). Its quarterly set is the only way to see the run-off of the stavební spoření book as it is absorbed into KB.

source_name: Artesa, spořitelní družstvo — Povinně uveřejňované informace
why_relevant: Best-documented example of the cell's full value proposition at a small institution: confirmed quarterly XLSX disclosures explicitly covering capital adequacy, member/shareholder structure, organisational chart and branch and staff counts, quarterly cadence, archive back to 2007, latest 31.3.2026 posted 11.6.2026. For an entity of this size there is no other structured public financial record at all.

source_name: Citfin spořitelní družstvo — Povinně uveřejňované informace
why_relevant: FX/payments-focused credit union — directly on-sector for the payments half of the run. Confirmed quarterly XLSX under Decree 163/2014 plus separate CRR Art. 575/2013 and Banking-Act streams, latest 30.6.2026, archive to 2006, audited annual reports with related-party disclosures. Its sister entity Citfin - Finanční trhy, a.s. discloses on a parallel page under the securities-dealer regime, giving a two-sided view of one payments group.

source_name: NEY spořitelní družstvo — Veřejné informace
why_relevant: Confirms the cell's headline claim that the template exposes soft organisational data nowhere else public: alongside capital-adequacy annexes it publishes a downloadable organisational-structure spreadsheet and an explicit FTE headcount (21 FTE in 2025). Quarterly/semi-annual XLSX, latest observed 30.6.2025, annual accounts back to 2011.

source_name: Peněžní dům, spořitelní družstvo — Povinně uveřejňované informace
why_relevant: Recovered URL: the ČNB-listed http://www.peneznidum.cz/povinne-informace.html 404s, but the site root's own navigation exposes a current path under /informace/. Small regional credit union with no other structured public reporting; also completes the credit-union tier of the cell.

source_name: Podnikatelská družstevní záložna (penezniustav.cz) — mandatory disclosures
why_relevant: The sixth credit union in the ČNB index; the regulator gives only the site root rather than a deep link, so the disclosure corner has to be located from the site's own navigation. Included for completeness of the deposit-taking universe.

source_name: Stavebky.cz — Přehledy / statistiky stavebního spoření
why_relevant: Third-party aggregator that appears to compile the quarterly figures the building societies publish under Decree 163/2014 into cross-institution comparison tables. If it holds, it is a ready-made cross-check on our own parsing of the primary XLSX files and a fallback when an individual society's site is unreachable. Discovered as a search hit while chasing ČSOB Stavební spořitelna; not yet fetched, so treat scope and provenance as unconfirmed.
